<!-- Source: docs/agent-guide/README.md -->

# Talox: choose the browser operation first

Talox is a local, stateful browser runtime for agents. This guide describes the checked-out **v9.0.1** source (not the older v9.0.0 baseline). Start with structured state; escalate to screenshots or vision when the page requires it. Keep one controller alive across actions and always stop it in `finally`.

| I need to… | Choose this operation, with these arguments | Recipe |
|---|---|---|
| Read a page | `await t.navigate(url)` then `await t.getState('agent')` | [Read](browsing.md#read-and-observe) |
| Get the full contract or diagnostics | `t.getState('full')` / `t.getState('debug')` | [State](browsing.md#read-and-observe) |
| Click or type resiliently | `t.click('#save')`, `t.type('#name', 'Ada')`; inspect `failed` | [Actions](browsing.md#click-type-and-fill-forms) |
| Fill a form | Type each field, click submit, verify the resulting state | [Forms](browsing.md#click-type-and-fill-forms) |
| Keep a login | Reuse the same base directory, profile ID and profile class | [Profiles](browsing.md#reuse-a-profile-for-a-login) |
| Capture a screenshot | `t.screenshot({path})` or `t.annotatedScreenshot()` | [Capture](browsing.md#screenshots-and-pdfs) |
| Print a PDF | `t.getPlaywrightPage().pdf({path, format:'A4', printBackground:true})` | [PDF](browsing.md#screenshots-and-pdfs) |
| Scrape a table / page summary | `t.extractTable('#prices')` / `getPracticalTools(t).extractVisibleStructuredContent()` | [Scraping](browsing.md#extract-data) |
| Reach an iframe | `t.getPlaywrightPage().frameLocator('iframe')`; assess cross-origin trust separately | [Frames](orchestration.md#iframes-reachability-and-trust) |
| Open another tab | `t.openPage(url)`, `t.switchPage(0)`, `t.closePage(1)` | [Tabs](orchestration.md#tabs) |
| Run independent browser workers | Separate controllers and profile IDs; fixed actions with `Promise.all` | [Workers](orchestration.md#parallel-browser-workers) |
| Ask an LLM to coordinate workers | CLI `run` with goal, `--agents N`, `--max-iterations N`, model/API configuration | [Planning](orchestration.md#llm-planned-runs) |
| Debug / replay a failure | Record at launch; `replay <session-dir> --output <html>` | [Replay](orchestration.md#record-debug-and-replay) |
| Use a local vision server | `createLocalVisionReasoner({provider:'ollama', model, baseUrl})`; `t.useVision(reasoner)` | [Vision](integrations.md#local-vision) |
| Expose browser tools to an agent | CLI `mcp` over newline-delimited stdio JSON-RPC | [MCP](integrations.md#mcp) |
| Add rules / visual detectors | `registerTaloxPlugin({name, version, rules, visionDetectors})` | [Plugins](integrations.md#plugins-and-platform-adapters) |
| Get platform-specific guidance | `matchPlatformAdapters(url, title)` from `talox/adapters` | [Adapters](integrations.md#plugins-and-platform-adapters) |

## Run the recipes

From this checkout, build with `npm run build`, then run `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs`. Select one recipe by appending its name, for example `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs form`. The [executable source](examples.mjs) supplies a local `file://` fixture, temporary profiles, assertions, cleanup and exact imports. Every recipe below links to one of these cases; [VERIFIED.md](VERIFIED.md) records actual results and distinguishes protocol fixtures from real inference.

In prose, `t` means the launched controller from that harness, `url` its fixture URL, `dir` its temporary directory. Replace the fixture with your authorized target for real work. In an installed consumer use `import { TaloxController } from 'talox'`; the checkout harness uses `../../dist/index.js` to test exactly the local build.

## Launch without macOS Keychain prompts

The recipes explicitly select **Playwright's bundled Chromium** and create a temporary profile directory. They never select the user's Google Chrome. This avoids the system-Chrome Keychain path.

**The v9.0.1 default is different:** `BrowserManager.buildLaunchOptions()` sets `channel: 'chrome'` when its own `adaptiveStealthEnabled` is true, and `ProfileVault` uses persistent directories. A bare CLI screenshot or MCP launch therefore cannot be promised to avoid system Chrome. Setting controller settings alone does not propagate to the manager's separate configuration in this revision. Before `launch`, the harness uses the exposed internal seam:

```js
// After constructing t, before launch; see examples.mjs controller().
t._session.browserManager.updateConfig({
  browser: { autoDetect: false, preferred: 'chromium', headless: true },
  settings: { adaptiveStealthEnabled: false, virtualDisplay: false },
});
```

This is a version-specific workaround, not a stable top-level controller option. Keep it while this source requires it. Install missing bundled binaries with `npx playwright install chromium`; never change the workspace's shared `node_modules` symlink. On Linux, select an intentional display configuration rather than copying the macOS headless recipe into a headed workflow.

## Know the boundaries

- `launch(profileId, profileClass, browserType, observeOptions?)` returns `Promise<void>`. Navigation, click and type return state; they often **return a `failed` object rather than throw**. Check it before taking the next action.
- The default `ops` policy permits Google, GitHub, `about:blank` and loopback hosts; `file://` fixtures use `qa`. `qa` and `sandbox` have broad default allowlists. Use the profile class your task authorizes.
- `type` appends text. No `fillForm`, `getPageState`, `annotatedPdf`, `talox launch`, or `LocalVisionReasoner` constructor exists on the advertised surface.
- Node.js 20+ is required. LLM planning needs an OpenAI-compatible endpoint/key; ordinary browser API operations do not.

[CLI arguments and defaults](cli-reference.md) · [Unexpected features](features.md) · [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) · [Machine-readable inventory](../capabilities.json) · [Agent skill](../../skills/talox/SKILL.md)

## Inventory and performance contract

Regenerate with `npm run docs:capabilities`. The generator uses the TypeScript AST/checker, resolves exports across all four entrypoints, reads MCP registrations reached by `src/cli/mcp.ts`, CLI parsers/dispatch/help normalization, presets, practical tools, JSON schemas and environment reads. It never imports executable Talox source. `source` is file:line at generation time.

Each entry has `id`, `kind`, `signature`, `arguments`, `returns`, `errors`, `source`, `useWhen` and `derived`. `null` defaults mean **not statically established**, not a promise of runtime null. Expression objects preserve unevaluated source. API member entries include overloads as separate source locations; `apiExports` counts only the public export names. `properties` expands object contracts up to two levels; named return types resolve through the API/schema inventory. Direct throw/tool-error sites are included; transitive browser/network exceptions are not exhaustively inferred.

`derived:false` and `notDerivable` are deliberate review queues: conditional CLI requiredness/positionals, environment-dependent defaults and unevaluated expressions need the linked source. The unit test prints this complete list and independently checks CLI routes/flags, MCP schemas and compiler-resolved exports. Do not turn unknown values into invented documentation.

This documentation adds no browser-runtime work. Generation is a one-shot compiler pass, no network and no polling. Maintenance budgets: generation under 30 s and 512 MiB RSS on a developer machine; unit inventory checks under 60 s each. Recipe waits are bounded (3 s for the fixture selector, 3 s for the local vision fixture, 20 s per CLI child); fixtures have no remote page resources. These are acceptance budgets, not a claim that a real website or model will respond within them.

# Read, act, capture and extract

## Read and observe

Run `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs read`.

The fixture harness constructs `new TaloxController(dir, {settings: {...PRESETS.ops, headed:false, safeMode:true, humanStealth:0, fidgetEnabled:false, automaticThinkingEnabled:false, autoHeadedEscalation:false, adaptiveStealthEnabled:false, navigationWaitUntil:'domcontentloaded'}})`, applies the bundled-browser workaround in the [overview](README.md), then calls `await t.launch('lab', 'qa', 'chromium')` and `await t.navigate(url)`. It calls `await t.stop()` in `finally`.

`navigate(url)` returns `TaloxPageState`. `getState('full')` returns the full contract, including nodes, interactive elements, console/network evidence, bugs, timing and optional `failed`. `getState('agent')` gives a compact view suitable for the next LLM decision. `getState('debug')` retains forensic evidence. Prefer compact state in the reasoning loop; collect full/debug only when needed. Node IDs and annotated screenshot refs are observation-local; click using the current CSS selector, not a guessed `@e1` selector.

Failure: an operation returns `state.failed` with `operation` and `reason`. Stop the action chain, inspect that reason and [troubleshoot](troubleshooting.md). A resolved promise alone is not success. Do not use the headed `observe` CLI for an unattended one-shot page read: it waits for a human-driven session to end. Its exact flags are [here](cli-reference.md).

## Click, type and fill forms

Run `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs interact` and `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs form`.

The action recipe calls `await t.waitForSelector('#save', 3000)`, `await t.findElement('Save', 'button')`, `await t.type('#name', 'Ada')`, then `await t.click('#save')`. `findElement` returns `{selector, boundingBox}` or null. Type and click return state and use Talox's reliability path; safe mode makes owned-fixture interactions deterministic. The form recipe types `'Test User'`, submits once and verifies `document.querySelector('#result').textContent` through `t.evaluate(script)`.

`type` appends; clear an existing field intentionally with the underlying page's locator `fill('')` before typing when replacement is required. This is an escape hatch, not a `fillForm` helper. Check validation messages and the final submitted state. Never blindly repeat a submit whose outcome is uncertain.

Failure: element missing, stale or outside the attention frame. Refresh state, use a current selector, wait for the intended element, or adjust the attention frame only if appropriate. Do not use a DOM click for canvas coordinates or inside a different frame; use the frame/vision path. Do not run human takeover in an unattended fixture test.

## Reuse a profile for a login

Run `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs profile`.

The harness opens and stops the same `('persistent', 'qa', 'chromium')` profile twice under the same `dir`, writes a localStorage sentinel on the first pass and asserts it survives the second. This verifies persistence without accessing a real login. Real sessions need a durable base directory rather than the fixture's temporary directory; keep the same profile ID and class. Use a separate directory/ID for each concurrently active browser.

Return: `launch`/`stop` resolve void; subsequent navigation returns state with persisted storage applied. Common failure: `PROFILE_IN_USE` means another context owns the directory. Stop that owner or use a different profile; do not remove a live lock. Do not use a temporary fixture profile when you need tomorrow's login. A real human login can use headed mode and `requestHumanTakeover(reason)`; no credentials belong in guide examples.

## Screenshots and PDFs

Run `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs screenshot` and `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs pdf`.

`await t.screenshot({path: path.join(dir, 'page.png')})` captures the page; optional `selector` crops an element. The return is `Buffer | string` (the implementation may return a path when writing). `await t.annotatedScreenshot()` returns PNG bytes with numbered element refs; write them with `fs.writeFile`. The recipe checks the PNG header.

For PDF, `await t.getPlaywrightPage().pdf({path: path.join(dir, 'page.pdf'), format:'A4', printBackground:true})` uses the already-launched Chromium page and returns PDF bytes. The recipe checks `%PDF`. Talox has no PDF CLI or `annotatedPdf` method. This public page escape hatch keeps the same session/profile; PDF support is Chromium-specific.

Failure: no active page or navigation error. Launch and check `navigate().failed` before capture. Do not use a screenshot as evidence that a submit succeeded; verify the resulting state too. Do not invoke the default screenshot CLI when you require the bundled-browser guarantee described in the overview. Do not try Chromium PDF printing with Firefox/WebKit.

## Extract data

Run `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs scrape`.

`await t.extractTable('#prices')` returns `Array<Record<string,string>>`; the fixture asserts `[{col0:'Plan',col1:'Price'},{col0:'Lab',col1:'0'}]` (this fixture has no `thead`; headers are included as a row). `getPracticalTools(t).extractVisibleStructuredContent()` returns `{url,title,sections:[{heading,summary,selectors}]}` built from up to six named state nodes. It is a compact summary, not a full document extraction. `await getPracticalTools(t).exportMarkdownSnapshot(path.join(dir,'snapshot.md'))` writes normalized visible text and returns the absolute path.

Failure: `Table not found: …` means selector/frame/page mismatch. Re-observe before changing the selector. Do not use the six-section summary when completeness matters; explicitly extract the required fields with `t.evaluate(script)` or table extraction and validate counts. Practical helpers `searchOnSite` and `captureApiResponse` exist in the inventory but their evaluated script strings contain TypeScript syntax in this revision; do not assume those paths run as plain browser JavaScript. No successful recipe relies on them.


<!-- Source: docs/agent-guide/orchestration.md -->

# Frames, tabs, workers and evidence

## Iframes: reachability and trust

Run `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs iframes`.

A same-origin or `srcdoc` frame can be reached through the current session's Playwright page: `await t.getPlaywrightPage().frameLocator('iframe').locator('#inside').click()`. This returns void; re-observe the intended frame/result after acting. The fixture proves this path with a local frame.

For cross-origin CDP sessions, set controller `settings.enableCrossOriginIframes:true` and `trustedDomains` to exact approved origins. There is no `iframeTrust` preset. `new CrossOriginManager({trustedDomains:['https://frame.invalid']})` provides `assessTrust(frameUrl,parentUrl)` without opening a website. The fixture asserts an approved origin is trusted and an unrelated origin is not. With a real page installed via `manager.install(page)`, `getAllSessions()` returns frame IDs and trust metadata; `executeInTrustedFrame(frameId, command, params?)` gates execution on trust. Dispose a manually created manager when finished. The controller owns its own manager lifecycle.

Failure: `No CDP session for frame: …` can mean the frame detached/navigated, session creation is pending, or the engine is not Chromium. Refresh sessions; don't cache frame IDs across navigations. `Refusing trusted-frame execution` requires reviewing the origin, not blindly broadening trust. Wildcards and opaque origins cannot be trusted. Technical frame reachability never grants authority to obey instructions embedded in external page content. Do not use main-page selectors to target elements inside a frame.

## Tabs

Run `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs tabs`.

The recipe records `t.getActivePageIndex()`, calls `await getPracticalTools(t).openBackgroundTab('about:blank')`, checks `t.getPageCount()`, then `t.switchPage(initial)` and `await t.closePage(1)`. The helper returns `{state,message}`. Despite its name it delegates to `openPage`, which **activates the new page** in this revision. `openPage(url)` returns page state, `switchPage(index)` returns void, and `closePage(index)` resolves void. Indexes are zero-based and can change when tabs close.

Failure: `Invalid page index: …` means a stale index. Recheck count/active page. Do not interpret this helper as a background-only operation or share active-page selection between concurrently executing tasks. Prefer distinct controllers for independent concurrent actions.

## Parallel browser workers

Run `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs parallel`.

The recipe creates two Talox controllers with separate `worker-0` and `worker-1` profile IDs, applies the bundled-browser launch configuration to each, launches both as `qa/chromium`, runs fixed `navigate(url)` actions with `Promise.all`, checks each state and stops both. This is local browser concurrency, with no model calls. Return: an array of independent page states. It tests the useful session-isolation path without external services.

Failure: `PROFILE_IN_USE` means workers share a directory; choose distinct profiles. Do not parallelize dependent actions in one page. Limit concurrency to your real CPU/RAM budget and target's permitted load. Two workers are a fixture choice, not a recommended default for every machine.

## LLM-planned runs

Run `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs cli-options` to exercise the real parser/help route for `run 'Read title' --agents 2 --max-iterations 1 --help`. This is explicitly a **help-only** check, not a model-driven browser run.

For production, `talox run` takes a required goal, optional `--url` start page, `--model` (default `gpt-4o`), `--api-key` or `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `--base-url` or (multi-agent path) `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `--max-iterations` (10), `--strategy` (`balanced`), `--skills-dir`, and `--agents` (1). Counts greater than one select `PlanDelegateObserveLoop` and `AgentCoordinator`; `--agents=N` is also recognized. The CLI emits progress/results and a process exit status, not a raw page-state response. The current default launch selection caveat applies to these commands.

`AgentCoordinator` offers deterministic task waves (`navigate`, `click`, `type`, `getState`, `screenshot`, `wait`) and shared-state result keys with `first-write-wins`, `last-write-wins` or `reject` conflict handling. `PlanDelegateObserveLoop` adds observation and replanning with explicit stop reasons. Use the [manifest](../capabilities.json) for the full typed contracts before authoring a custom runtime.

Failure: missing goal/key is rejected before execution; LLM HTTP failures appear as `LLM API error: …`. Configure an authorized compatible model endpoint. Do not use LLM planning for an already-known selector sequence, or describe parser-help verification as real model execution. The offline guide does not exercise paid planning, real login, live cross-origin CDP execution or the default coordinator launch path.

## Record, debug and replay

Run `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs replay`.

The recipe passes the fourth launch argument `{headed:false, overlay:false, record:true, output:'both', outputDir:reports}`. It performs a real local click, calls `stop()` to flush the observe report, discovers the report directory, then executes the built CLI with `['replay', sessionDir, '--output', outputPath]`. It verifies the resulting HTML. Report formats are `json`, `markdown` and `both`; the return of `stop()` is void, and evidence lives on disk.

`talox replay [session-dir | report.json] [--output path] [--open]` builds an offline HTML viewer. No input selects the newest session under `./talox-sessions`. It returns an output path on stdout and exit status; it does not rerun browser actions. Avoid `--open` in unattended/macOS runs because it invokes the system browser. For immediate diagnosis, `await t.getDebugSnapshot()` returns the latest state, bugs, console/network failures and last adaptation; `getState('debug')` collects current evidence.

Failure: `Invalid Talox session report: …` means the wrong file or an invalid/incomplete report. Use the observe session's `report.json`, not arbitrary state JSON; finish `stop()` first. A replay without screenshots can still be valid if capture failed or was disabled. Do not treat replay HTML as proof of a successful rerun.


<!-- Source: docs/agent-guide/integrations.md -->

# Connect an agent or extend the runtime

## MCP

Run `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs mcp-stdio` for the real built stdio server and `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs mcp` for all seven real tool handlers using a controller factory configured for bundled Chromium. The latter uses the built internal `TaloxMcpSession` test seam, not an installed package subpath export. The default stdio server factory has the system-Chrome caveat from the [overview](README.md).

An MCP host starts the executable `talox` with the single argument `mcp` in the intended working directory. The transport is **one JSON-RPC object per line**, not HTTP or Content-Length framing. stdout belongs exclusively to MCP responses; diagnostics use stderr. Server shutdown/EOF stops its active browser. The stdio fixture sends `tools/list`, closes stdin and asserts seven registrations and exit 0 without launching a browser.

| Tool | Exact arguments in the browser fixture | Return |
|---|---|---|
| `talox_launch` | `{profileId:'mcp-lab', profileClass:'qa', browser:'chromium'}` | Text JSON `{launched:true,profileId,profileClass,browser}` |
| `talox_navigate` | `{url}` (fixture file URL) | Text JSON page state |
| `talox_type` | `{selector:'#name',text:'MCP'}` | Text JSON page state |
| `talox_click` | `{selector:'#save'}` | Text JSON page state |
| `talox_state` | `{variant:'agent'}` | Text JSON state (default **agent**) |
| `talox_screenshot` | `{selector:'#save'}` | `content:[{type:'image',data:<base64>,mimeType:'image/png'}]` |
| `talox_stop` | `{}` | Text JSON `{stopped:true}`; false if already stopped |

The browser fixture initializes protocol `2025-11-25` with `capabilities:{}` and `clientInfo:{name:'guide',version:'1'}`, lists tools, launches, navigates, types, clicks, collects state, captures PNG and stops. Legacy initialization supports `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26`, `2024-11-05`. Modern clients use `server/discover` and protocol `2026-07-28` metadata; the server adds complete-result metadata. See registration schemas in [capabilities.json](../capabilities.json) for required fields, enums and `additionalProperties:false`.

Common failure: `No active Talox MCP browser session. Call talox_launch first.` Launch once before actions; stop before relaunching. `isError:true` denotes a tool failure, while malformed/unknown calls can return JSON-RPC errors. Navigation can embed `failed` inside successful text content, so parse and inspect it too. Do not pass API-only parameters such as screenshot `path`: this MCP tool accepts only `selector`. The general `getTaloxTools()` function-calling schemas are a different surface: they use `talox_get_state`, whereas MCP uses `talox_state`.

## Local vision

Run `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs vision`.

The fixture starts an HTTP server on an ephemeral loopback port, calls `createLocalVisionReasoner({provider:'ollama',model:'fixture',baseUrl,timeoutMs:3000,maxTokens:64,keepAlive:0,allowRemote:false})`, installs it with `t.useVision(reasoner)`, then calls `await reasoner.analyze(await t.annotatedScreenshot(), 'Read the heading')`. The server verifies it received an image and returns a fixed answer. This verifies the real request/response wiring, **not model inference or answer quality**.

Return: a `VisualReasoner` with `name` and `analyze(Buffer,question):Promise<string|null>`. Empty model responses return null. Ollama defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:11434`, 60 s timeout and no explicit max-token override. `provider:'openai-compatible'` requires `baseUrl` (usually a local `/v1` endpoint), uses optional `apiKey`, and defaults to 300 maximum tokens. Load a real multimodal model in the local server before using a screenshot in production. `t.useVision(null)` removes the per-controller reasoner.

Failure: `Refusing non-loopback local vision endpoint …` means the host is not loopback. Correct the address; enable `allowRemote` only for intentional screenshot transfer. HTTP/invalid-JSON/timeouts are reported explicitly. Do not use local vision when structured DOM state already answers the question, or claim the fixture proves a real model understands a page.

## Plugins and platform adapters

Run `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs plugins` and `node docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs adapters`.

The plugin recipe imports `registerTaloxPlugin`, `listTaloxPlugins` and `unregisterTaloxPlugin` from `talox/plugins`. It registers `{name:'guide-lab',version:'1.0.0',rules:[{id:'lab-rule',analyze:()=>[]}]}`, asserts registry membership, then unregisters it. Registration returns `TaloxPluginInfo` (name, version and rule/detector IDs); unregister returns boolean. A real rule's `analyze(state)` returns bugs. Optional `visionDetectors` supply `{id,detect(context)}` and return visual detections. Register before the relevant collection/analysis, keep identifiers unique and clean up in tests.

Failure: duplicate plugin/rule/detector IDs are rejected, and plugin detector failures are isolated into result errors. Do not use a plugin as an unrestricted browser script loader; it supplies rules/detectors, not browser authority.

The adapter recipe imports `matchPlatformAdapters` from `talox/adapters` and calls `matchPlatformAdapters('https://github.com/AVANT-ICONIC/Talox/issues','Issues')`. This is **pure URL matching**, no network request. It returns matches with `adapterId`, name, kind, confidence, guidance and routes. Built-ins cover GitHub, WordPress admin, WooCommerce admin, Shopify admin and Slack; `PlatformAdapterRegistry` supports custom adapters. `getPlatformAdapterContext(url,title?)` returns guidance text.

Failure: a malformed/unsupported URL yields no matches; custom invalid adapters throw validation errors. Treat guidance as hints checked against live state. Do not interpret an adapter match as authentication, a ready-made scraper or an action executor. No `loadPlugin` or `getPlatformAdapter` function is exported.


<!-- Source: docs/agent-guide/cli-reference.md -->

# CLI arguments: parser truth

Use the installed `talox` executable, or `node dist/cli/entry.js` in this checkout. All flags below come from the current parsers. Full parser/execution source, conditional requirements and errors live in [capabilities.json](../capabilities.json). This table is a readable snapshot; regenerate the manifest and review this page when changing CLI source.

The executable harness checks each leaf command's help route (`cli-options`), top-level `--help` / `-h`, real `init`, real replay and stdio MCP. Help exits before browser/model startup. No live LLM call is claimed. The `skill` parent requires `create`; `talox launch` is not a command.

## Positional inputs and traps

| Command | Positional input / constraint |
|---|---|
| `observe` | No positional URL; opens a human-driven session and waits for closure |
| `init` | Optional directory; default `talox-app` (see source constant) |
| `screenshot` | Optional URL; absent means capture initial page; writes annotated PNG |
| `chat` | No goal positional; interactive LLM chat; `--url` is API base URL |
| `doctor` | No positional input; diagnostics include network/live-launch checks; `--fix` can install binaries/change config |
| `daemon` | No positional input; long-running local IPC service |
| `run` | Required goal, quoted as one shell argument; `--url` is start page |
| `research` | Required goal and `--domain`; experiments need a model/key |
| `skill create` | Required `--domain`, `--name`, `--description`, `--file`; writes a domain skill |
| `replay` | Optional session directory or `report.json`; absent chooses newest under `./talox-sessions` |
| `mcp` | No extra arguments except `--help`/`-h`; stdio server until EOF/shutdown |

Top-level `--help` and `-h` normalize to `init --help`. Some legacy leaf commands accept only `--help`; do not assume `-h` works everywhere. Most options require separate tokens, not `--flag=value`; the deliberate exception is `--agents=N`. The multi-agent path parses a subset of the run flags and ignores unknown options; misspellings can silently fall back to defaults. Use these exact spellings.

`OPENAI_API_KEY` provides an alternative to `--api-key`. `OPENAI_BASE_URL` is read in chat and multi-agent execution; single-agent run/research pass their parsed base URL instead. Chat parser's model default is `gpt-4o`, so do not assume `OPENAI_MODEL` overrides a nonempty CLI model. Environment behavior is recorded at every read site in the manifest.

## chat

| `--model` | `string` | `"gpt-4o"` | no |
| `--api-key` | `string  /  undefined` | `undefined` | no |
| `--url` | `string  /  undefined` | `undefined` | no |
| `--help` | `boolean` | `false` | no |
| `-h` | `boolean` | `false` | no |

## init

Source: `src/cli/talox.ts:1197`. Return: console output / process exit status.

| Argument | Type | Default | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--help` | `boolean` | `false` | no |
| `-h` | `boolean` | `false` | no |

# Features agents tend to miss

Use the [manifest](../capabilities.json) for exact signatures and source locations. This page is a discovery map, not a promise that every feature has been exercised offline. Tested recipes are enumerated in [VERIFIED.md](VERIFIED.md).

| Need you might overlook | Existing surface | Boundary / useful surprise |
|---|---|---|
| Spend fewer context tokens | `getState('agent')`, `getIntentState()`, `describePage()` | API defaults full; MCP defaults agent |
| Compare observations | `TALOX_STATE_CONTRACT_VERSION`, `diffPageState` | Structured changes, not screenshot-only guessing |
| Cheap observation before OCR/vision | `PerceptionStack`, `PERCEPTION_PRESETS` | Choose perception depth deliberately |
| See what was actually clicked | `annotatedScreenshot`, attention-frame helpers | Numbered labels are observations, not durable CSS selectors |
| Make fixture interaction deterministic | `setSafeMode(true)` | Bypasses human simulation; type still appends |
| Detect CAPTCHA/login/consent obstacles | `getChallengeState`, `resolveChallenge`, `ChallengeDetector` | `requiresHuman` is an explicit outcome, not success |
| Hand control to the user | `requestHumanTakeover`, takeover history/events | Headed workflow; configure timeout; unsuitable unattended |
| Reuse a real identity | `ProfileVault`, profile-specific fingerprints | Separate persistent ownership from settings presets |
| Keep page state over a browser restart | `captureSessionSnapshot`, `restoreSessionSnapshot`, headed-mode transition | Session snapshot contains more than just URL |
| Learn strategies for a hostname | `AdaptationEngine`, `DomainMemory`, `STRATEGIES` | Per-domain strategy history; not an authorization mechanism |
| Recover selectors and interactions | `InteractionReliability` and self-healing controller actions | Inspect failures after recovery instead of assuming success |
| Handle interstitial warmup | `SiteWarmupRegistry`, `BUILT_IN_WARMUPS` | Registry strategies are site-dependent and can become stale |
| Handle browser dialogs | `AutoDialogHandler`, `autoDialogHandling` setting | Know which dialogs may be auto-handled before a risky action |
| Record a forensic session | Launch observe options, `ObserveSession`, `SessionReporter` | Reports flush on stop; replay reads persisted reports |
| Capture network traffic | `HarRecorder`, controller `harRecording` config | Stop flushes; recording content can include sensitive data |
| Attach an inspect endpoint | `InspectServer`, controller `inspectServer` config | A live debugging surface, not an exported recording |
| Record video | `VideoRecorder`, controller `videoRecording`, launch `recordVideo` | Explicit recording paths; stop finalizes evidence |
| Carry origin-scoped headers | `OriginHeaders`, controller `originHeaders` | Scoped origin matching, not arbitrary cross-origin credential reuse |
| Reach external frames safely | `CrossOriginManager`, exact `trustedDomains` | Reachability and trust are separate; no wildcard trust |
| Export visible text to a file | `getPracticalTools(t).exportMarkdownSnapshot(dest)` | Normalized text, not a semantic HTML-to-Markdown renderer |
| Use a low-level page operation | `getPlaywrightPage()` | Same browser/profile, but direct operations bypass controller action evidence |
| Reuse common settings | `PRESETS.ops`, `.qa`, `.observe`, `.research`, `['login-heavy']` | Exactly five; preset names are not all profile classes |
| Run browser tasks concurrently | `AgentCoordinator`, deterministic shared-state merge | Multiple profiles, explicit result conflicts |
| Replan from all agents' observations | `PlanDelegateObserveLoop` | Wave history and typed stop reasons; model required by default |
| Stop a stuck autonomous loop | `AutonomousLoop` convergence/recovery | Bounded iteration budget matters even with self-learning |
| Load domain knowledge | `SkillLoader`, `SkillWriter`, `skill create` | Manifest/reference containment and registry reconciliation exist |
| Research strategies empirically | `AutoResearchLoop`, `ExperimentRunner`, `RegressionHarness`, `ResearchJournal`, `ResearchReporter` | Controlled experiments, promotion and rollback, not one blind rewrite |
| Transfer strategy hypotheses | `CrossDomainTransfer`, `StrategyComposer`, `HypothesisGenerator` | Source-backed research features, not general scraping commands |
| Evolve prompts / skill versions | `PromptEvolver`, `SkillVersioning`, `SkillEvaluator`, `AdaptiveExperimentPriority` | Evaluate before promotion |
| Measure human-simulation quality | `QualityTracker`, `scoreInteraction`, `computeQuality` | Explicit metrics rather than aesthetic claims |
| Expose model function schemas | `getTaloxTools`, `getToolNames` | Different from the seven MCP registrations |
| Keep browser access in one local process | `TaloxDaemon` / CLI `daemon` | IPC lifecycle; separate from MCP transport |
| Load community rules/detectors | `talox/plugins` registry | Versioned names, duplicate validation, isolated detector errors |
| Get platform-specific hints | `talox/adapters` registry and five built-ins | Pure matching/guidance, no browser actions |
| Use an on-device model server | `talox/local-vision` factory | Rejects remote endpoints by default; no cloud call needed |
| Connect your own vision or CAPTCHA solver | `VisualReasoner`, `useVision`, `useSolver`, solver registry | Model/solver behavior and task authorization remain separate |
| Control content/network defenses | `contentSafety`, `networkGuard`, `trustedDomains` settings | Read the actual defaults and schemas before changing scope |
| Use a Linux virtual display | BrowserManager `virtualDisplay` / Xvfb lifecycle | Linux only; manager config propagation caveat applies |
| Enforce navigation/action rules | `PolicyEngine`, YAML policies, amount context | `ops` is intentionally restrictive; inspect a refusal |

The exhaustive names, types, defaults, public members, environment reads and raw JSON state schema are in the generated inventory. No module name in this page implies a CLI command exists with that spelling.


<!-- Source: docs/agent-guide/troubleshooting.md -->

# Diagnose the observed failure

Start with `state.failed` after navigation/click/type; those operations catch errors into the state contract. Preserve the failing selector/URL, current state, profile class and operation. Screenshot/report helpers may throw instead. MCP adds tool errors and JSON-RPC errors around the state contract.

These messages were extracted from current throw/tool-error sites (not guessed from README prose). Each link leads to the implementing source; exact line references and the complete direct-throw inventory are also in [capabilities.json](../capabilities.json), top-level `errors`. Browser/OS/network exceptions can add messages beyond that inventory.

| Message / substring | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Policy Violation: URL … not allowed for … profile` | Profile navigation policy refuses this URL | Inspect the policy and target; use an authorized class/policy. Local file fixtures use `qa`. Do not assume `ops` permits every site. [ActionExecutor](../../src/core/controller/ActionExecutor.ts) |
| `Policy Violation: Action 'click' … blocked` / `Action 'type' … blocked` | Action policy refuses target | Review intended action and policy before retrying; changing the selector is not a policy bypass. [ActionExecutor](../../src/core/controller/ActionExecutor.ts) |
| `Human-in-the-Loop blocked risky action` | Risky operation needs human involvement | Arrange authorized takeover in a headed session; stop unattended execution at this boundary. [ActionExecutor](../../src/core/controller/ActionExecutor.ts) |
| `Element '…' not found within attention frame` | Target is outside the current allowed viewport region | Re-observe; adjust/clear frame only when intended. [ActionExecutor](../../src/core/controller/ActionExecutor.ts) |
| `Element not found: …` / `Table not found: …` | Wrong selector, page, frame or timing | Wait for a specific current selector, check active tab/frame, then retry the read. [ActionExecutor](../../src/core/controller/ActionExecutor.ts) |
| `No active page. Use launch() or openPage() first.` | Session not launched or page closed | Launch once before operations; stop only after evidence is collected. [SessionManager](../../src/core/controller/SessionManager.ts) |
| `Invalid page index: …` | Tab index no longer exists | Check page count and select a valid zero-based index. [SessionManager](../../src/core/controller/SessionManager.ts) |
| `Baseline '…' not found and autoSave is false.` | Visual comparison has no baseline | Deliberately create the baseline using `verifyVisual(key,true)` after reviewing the expected page. [SessionManager](../../src/core/controller/SessionManager.ts) |
| `PROFILE_IN_USE: Persistent profile is already active in this process` | Concurrent launches share a persistent directory | Await owner `stop()` or allocate another profile. [BrowserManager](../../src/core/BrowserManager.ts) |
| `LAUNCH_IN_PROGRESS: Browser launch is already in progress for this manager.` | Overlapping launch calls | Await the first launch; use separate managers for independent browsers. [BrowserManager](../../src/core/BrowserManager.ts) |
| `Browser launch failed for … Please ensure Chrome is installed.` | Default adaptive path selected system Chrome | For a bundled-only workflow configure the manager before launch as shown in the overview; install bundled Chromium if absent. [BrowserManager](../../src/core/BrowserManager.ts) |
| `Browser not launched` | Direct manager page operation before launch | Create the browser context first. [BrowserManager](../../src/core/BrowserManager.ts) |
| `Xvfb virtual display is only supported on Linux.` / `Xvfb not found` | Wrong platform or missing display binary | Use headless on macOS; on Linux install/configure Xvfb when a virtual headed display is intended. [BrowserManager](../../src/core/BrowserManager.ts) |
| `No free X display available in the :99-:199 range.` | Virtual display allocation exhausted | Release owned sessions/displays; investigate leaked owners rather than looping launch. [BrowserManager](../../src/core/BrowserManager.ts) |
| `No CDP session for frame: …` | Detached/unsupported/not-yet-attached frame | Refresh session list and use Chromium for CDP. [CrossOriginManager](../../src/core/CrossOriginManager.ts) |
| `Refusing trusted-frame execution` | Frame origin failed the trust gate | Review exact origin and authorized trust configuration. [CrossOriginManager](../../src/core/CrossOriginManager.ts) |
| `Wildcard trusted domains are not supported` / `Opaque origins cannot be trusted` | Trust configuration is too broad or unrepresentable | Supply explicit non-opaque origins; scheme and port matter. [CrossOriginManager](../../src/core/CrossOriginManager.ts) |
| `No active Talox MCP browser session. Call talox_launch first.` | MCP tool before launch | Call `talox_launch` once. [MCP server](../../src/core/mcp/TaloxMcpServer.ts) |
| `A Talox MCP browser session is already active. Stop it before relaunching.` | Duplicate MCP launch | `talox_stop` then launch. [MCP server](../../src/core/mcp/TaloxMcpServer.ts) |
| `Unexpected argument…` / `variant must be one of: agent, debug, full.` | Input does not match tool schema | Use `tools/list` schemas; do not mix MCP and API argument shapes. [MCP server](../../src/core/mcp/TaloxMcpServer.ts) |
| `Unknown Talox tool: …` | Wrong tool name | MCP state is `talox_state`; generic function schema state is `talox_get_state`. [MCP server](../../src/core/mcp/TaloxMcpServer.ts) |
| `No Talox sessions found in …` / `Unknown replay option: …` | Wrong working directory/input or flag | Supply an explicit observe session path and `--output` path. [Replay CLI](../../src/cli/replay.ts) |
| `Invalid Talox session report: …` / `Invalid Talox replay artifact: …` | Wrong/incomplete JSON report or malformed sidecar | Await report flush and use the matching session artifacts. [Replay loader](../../src/core/replay/ReplayLoader.ts) |
| `LLM API error: …` | Planner endpoint returned non-success | Check model, key and compatible base URL; do not repeat browser actions blindly. [Planner](../../src/core/loop/Planner.ts) |
| `Refusing non-loopback local vision endpoint` | Local mode targets another host | Point to the local server or explicitly authorize remote screenshot transfer. [Local vision](../../src/core/LocalVisionReasoner.ts) |
| `Local vision request timed out after …ms.` | Local inference exceeded the configured bound | Check server/model readiness, reduce request size or intentionally adjust timeout. [Local vision](../../src/core/LocalVisionReasoner.ts) |
| `Local vision server returned HTTP …` / `invalid JSON` | Wrong service/API path or bad server response | Verify provider, base URL and server protocol. [Local vision](../../src/core/LocalVisionReasoner.ts) |
| `Duplicate rule id … in plugin.` / `already registered by another plugin` | Registry ID collision | Use unique stable IDs and unregister test plugins. [Plugin registry](../../src/core/plugins/PluginRegistry.ts) |
| `adapter.id must be a lowercase identifier` / `adapter.guidance must contain non-empty strings.` | Invalid custom adapter | Follow `PlatformAdapter` contract; matching adapters contribute guidance only. [Adapter registry](../../src/core/platform/PlatformAdapterRegistry.ts) |

## Symptoms without an exception

A blank screenshot can follow ignored navigation failure. Inspect state before capture; the screenshot CLI now exits nonzero on a returned navigation failure. A correct-looking replay can still contain unsuccessful actions: inspect failures and network/console evidence. A resolved MCP tool call can contain a page state's `failed` object.

`type` appending twice is not self-healing failure: it is append semantics. A tab apparently changing after `openBackgroundTab` is current `openPage` activation behavior. A system-Chrome/Keychain prompt means the bundled-only manager workaround was not applied; controller `adaptiveStealthEnabled:false` alone does not change the manager's separately initialized config in v9.0.1.

If `searchOnSite` or `captureApiResponse` throws a browser JavaScript syntax error, inspect the evaluated strings in [practical-tools.ts](../../src/tools/practical-tools.ts): they contain TypeScript syntax. Prefer the verified table/summary/text paths for this revision; this documentation lane does not modify runtime source.

## Repository validation

- `npm run build`: exit 0.
- `npm run docs:capabilities`: exit 0; deterministic source-generated manifest.
- Targeted Vitest manifest suite: exit 0, 5/5 tests. Checks byte-for-byte freshness, independent CLI route/flag completeness, actual MCP registrations/schemas, compiler-resolved exports, source locations, portable type rendering and the unresolved-entry list.
- Full `npm run test:unit`: exit 1 due to existing doctor timeouts; see baseline comparison below. No runtime source was changed to hide these failures.
- `git diff --check`: exit 0.

The final full lane run at 10:24 reported **200 passing / 2 failing files**, **2,213 passing / 2 failing / 5 skipped tests**, plus the doctor beforeAll hook timeout. Both failing doctor CLI tests reproduced on `02b2281` in a source-only temporary baseline with the same dependency symlink and the unchanged build: `tests/unit/cli/talox.test.ts:92` and `:102` timed out at 30 s (27 other tests passed). A full baseline run then reproduced the separate `tests/unit/cli/doctor.test.ts:156` hook timeout and the `:102` CLI timeout: **199 passing / 2 failing files**, **2,209 passing / 1 failing / 5 skipped tests**. The timeout set varies between runs; all three observed doctor failures exist on the base source. The new five-test manifest suite passes independently.

The generator was measured with `/usr/bin/time -l node scripts/gen-capabilities.mjs --output /tmp/talox-capabilities-timed.json`: 2.54 s wall, 407,584,768 bytes maximum RSS (389 MiB), within the documented 30 s / 512 MiB maintenance budget. It performs no network requests. These timings describe this machine/run, not a universal runtime guarantee.

## Manifest counts and uncertainty

12 CLI dispatch entries (including the `skill` parent), 7 MCP tools, 309 public exports across four package entrypoints, 712 total API entries including public methods/practical functions, 5 settings presets, 10 named environment variables plus one whole-environment read, and 1 JSON schema.

28 entries are explicitly `derived:false`; all remain in the manifest with source/reasons. They are the 12 CLI entries (conditional/positional inference is partial), 10 named environment entries (no single global default), and these six API entries with unevaluated default expressions:

- `adapters:PlatformAdapterRegistry`
- `adapters:PlatformAdapterRegistry.constructor@235`
- `index:AgentCoordinator.setSharedValue@401`
- `index:createVLMCaptchaSolver`
- `index:SessionReporter`
- `index:SessionReporter.constructor@50`

The unit test lists every unresolved ID, and the manifest's `notDerivable` array is the authoritative complete list. No unknown default or transitive exception behavior is presented as a proven fact.


<!-- Source: docs/agent-guide/examples.mjs -->

## Complete executable recipe source

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
/** Offline executable recipes. Run from any directory; never selects installed Chrome. */
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL, fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { spawnSync, spawn } from 'node:child_process';
import http from 'node:http';
import { once } from 'node:events';
import { TaloxController, CrossOriginManager, getPracticalTools, PRESETS, setLogLevel } from '../../dist/index.js';
import { registerTaloxPlugin, unregisterTaloxPlugin, listTaloxPlugins } from '../../dist/plugins.js';
import { matchPlatformAdapters } from '../../dist/adapters.js';
import { createLocalVisionReasoner } from '../../dist/local-vision.js';
import { TaloxMcpSession } from '../../dist/core/mcp/TaloxMcpServer.js';

const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '../..');
const cli = path.join(root, 'dist/cli/entry.js');
const dir = await fs.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'talox-guide-'));
const fixture = path.join(dir, 'fixture.html');
await fs.writeFile(fixture, `<!doctype html><html lang="en"><title>Talox lab</title>
<h1>Local browser lab</h1><label>Name <input id="name"></label>
<button id="save" onclick="document.querySelector('#result').textContent=document.querySelector('#name').value">Save</button>
<p id="result" role="status">Ready</p><table id="prices"><tr><th>Plan</th><th>Price</th></tr><tr><td>Lab</td><td>0</td></tr></table>
<iframe title="Local frame" srcdoc="<button id='inside'>Inside</button>"></iframe></html>`);
const url = pathToFileURL(fixture).href;
setLogLevel('silent');

function controller(id = 'lab') {
  const t = new TaloxController(dir, { settings: {
    ...PRESETS.ops, headed: false, safeMode: true, humanStealth: 0,
    fidgetEnabled: false, automaticThinkingEnabled: false, autoHeadedEscalation: false,
    adaptiveStealthEnabled: false, navigationWaitUntil: 'domcontentloaded',
  } });
  // v9.0.1: controller settings do not propagate to BrowserManager's separate config.
  // This exported-but-internal seam is required to guarantee bundled Chromium.
  t._session.browserManager.updateConfig({
    browser: { autoDetect: false, preferred: 'chromium', headless: true },
    settings: { adaptiveStealthEnabled: false, virtualDisplay: false },
  });
  return { t, id };
}
function healthy(state) { assert.equal(state.failed, undefined, JSON.stringify(state.failed)); return state; }
async function browser(fn, id = 'lab', observe) {
  const { t } = controller(id);
  try {
    await t.launch(id, 'qa', 'chromium', observe);
    healthy(await t.navigate(url));
    await fn(t);
  } finally { await t.stop(); }
}
function command(args, expected = 0) {
  const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, [cli, ...args], { cwd: dir, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 20_000 });
  assert.equal(result.status, expected, result.stderr + result.stdout);
  return result.stdout;
}
const examples = {
  'cli-help': async () => { assert.match(command(['--help']), /talox observe/); },
  'cli-alias': async () => { assert.match(command(['-h']), /talox observe/); },
  'cli-init': async () => { command(['init', path.join(dir, 'scaffold')]); assert.ok((await fs.readdir(path.join(dir, 'scaffold'))).length); },
  'cli-options': async () => {
    for (const args of [['observe', '--help'], ['screenshot', '--help'], ['chat', '--help'], ['doctor', '--help'], ['daemon', '--help'], ['run', 'Read title', '--agents', '2', '--max-iterations', '1', '--help'], ['research', '--help'], ['skill', 'create', '--help'], ['mcp', '--help'], ['replay', '--help']]) command(args);
  },
  'read': () => browser(async t => {
    const state = healthy(await t.getState('full'));
    assert.equal(state.title, 'Talox lab'); assert.ok(state.nodes.length > 0);
    const agent = healthy(await t.getState('agent'));
    assert.ok(agent.interactiveElements.length > 0);
    const debug = healthy(await t.getState('debug')); assert.ok(debug.nodes.length > 0);
  }),
  'interact': () => browser(async t => {
    await t.waitForSelector('#save', 3000);
    const match = await t.findElement('Save', 'button'); assert.ok(match);
    healthy(await t.type('#name', 'Ada'));
    healthy(await t.click('#save'));
    assert.equal(await t.evaluate("document.querySelector('#result').textContent"), 'Ada');
  }),
  'form': () => browser(async t => {
    healthy(await t.type('#name', 'Test User'));
    healthy(await t.click('#save'));
    assert.equal(await t.evaluate("document.querySelector('#result').textContent"), 'Test User');
  }),
  'profile': async () => {
    await browser(async t => { await t.evaluate("localStorage.setItem('guide-profile', 'persisted')"); }, 'persistent');
    await browser(async t => { assert.equal(await t.evaluate("localStorage.getItem('guide-profile')"), 'persisted'); }, 'persistent');
  },
  'screenshot': () => browser(async t => {
    const raw = await t.screenshot({ path: path.join(dir, 'page.png') }); assert.ok(raw);
    const png = await t.annotatedScreenshot(); assert.equal(png.subarray(1, 4).toString(), 'PNG');
    await fs.writeFile(path.join(dir, 'annotated.png'), png);
  }),
  'pdf': () => browser(async t => {
    const pdf = await t.getPlaywrightPage().pdf({ path: path.join(dir, 'page.pdf'), format: 'A4', printBackground: true });
    assert.equal(pdf.subarray(0, 4).toString(), '%PDF');
  }),
  'scrape': () => browser(async t => {
    assert.deepEqual(await t.extractTable('#prices'), [{ col0: 'Plan', col1: 'Price' }, { col0: 'Lab', col1: '0' }]);
    const tools = getPracticalTools(t);
    const content = await tools.extractVisibleStructuredContent(); assert.equal(content.title, 'Talox lab');
    assert.ok(content.sections.length);
    const dest = await tools.exportMarkdownSnapshot(path.join(dir, 'snapshot.md'));
    assert.match(await fs.readFile(dest, 'utf8'), /Local browser lab/);
  }),
  'iframes': () => browser(async t => {
    const manager = new CrossOriginManager({ trustedDomains: ['https://frame.invalid'] });
    const trust = manager.assessTrust('https://frame.invalid/view', 'https://parent.invalid');
    assert.equal(trust.trusted, true);
    assert.equal(manager.assessTrust('https://other.invalid', 'https://parent.invalid').trusted, false);
    await t.getPlaywrightPage().frameLocator('iframe').locator('#inside').click();
    manager.dispose();
  }),
  'tabs': () => browser(async t => {
    const initial = t.getActivePageIndex();
    const result = await getPracticalTools(t).openBackgroundTab('about:blank'); healthy(result.state);
    assert.equal(t.getPageCount(), 2);
    // Despite the helper name, openPage activates the new tab in v9.0.1.
    t.switchPage(initial); assert.equal(healthy(await t.getState()).title, 'Talox lab');
    await t.closePage(1);
  }),
  'parallel': async () => {
    // Two independent browser runtimes, fixed tasks, no LLM service or agent delegation.
    const workers = [controller('worker-0').t, controller('worker-1').t];
    try {
      await Promise.all(workers.map((t, i) => t.launch(`worker-${i}`, 'qa', 'chromium')));
      const states = await Promise.all(workers.map(t => t.navigate(url)));
      states.forEach(state => assert.equal(healthy(state).title, 'Talox lab'));
    } finally { await Promise.all(workers.map(t => t.stop())); }
  },
  'replay': async () => {
    const reports = path.join(dir, 'reports');
    await browser(async t => { healthy(await t.click('#save')); }, 'recorded', { headed: false, overlay: false, record: true, output: 'both', outputDir: reports });
    const sessions = await fs.readdir(reports, { withFileTypes: true });
    const session = sessions.find(entry => entry.isDirectory()); assert.ok(session);
    const output = path.join(dir, 'replay.html');
    command(['replay', path.join(reports, session.name), '--output', output]);
    assert.match(await fs.readFile(output, 'utf8'), /<!doctype html>/i);
  },
  'vision': () => browser(async t => {
    // A local protocol fixture proves wiring; it does not claim real model inference.
    const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
      assert.equal(req.url, '/api/chat');
      let body = ''; req.on('data', chunk => { body += chunk; });
      req.on('end', () => {
        const data = JSON.parse(body); assert.ok(data.messages[0].images[0]);
        res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json'); res.end(JSON.stringify({ message: { content: 'Local browser lab' } }));
      });
    });
    server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1'); await once(server, 'listening');
    try {
      const reasoner = createLocalVisionReasoner({ provider: 'ollama', model: 'fixture', baseUrl: `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}`, timeoutMs: 3000, maxTokens: 64, keepAlive: 0, allowRemote: false });
      t.useVision(reasoner);
      assert.equal(await reasoner.analyze(await t.annotatedScreenshot(), 'Read the heading'), 'Local browser lab');
    } finally { await new Promise(resolve => server.close(resolve)); }
  }),
  'plugins': async () => {
    const info = registerTaloxPlugin({ name: 'guide-lab', version: '1.0.0', rules: [{ id: 'lab-rule', analyze: () => [] }] });
    assert.equal(info.name, 'guide-lab'); assert.ok(listTaloxPlugins().some(p => p.name === 'guide-lab'));
    assert.equal(unregisterTaloxPlugin('guide-lab'), true);
  },
  'adapters': async () => {
    // URL matching only; never contacts this host.
    const matches = matchPlatformAdapters('https://github.com/AVANT-ICONIC/Talox/issues', 'Issues');
    assert.ok(matches.some(match => match.adapterId === 'github'));
  },
  'mcp': async () => {
    const session = new TaloxMcpSession(() => controller('mcp-lab').t);
    let id = 0;
    async function request(method, params) {
      const response = await session.handle({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: ++id, method, params });
      assert.equal(response.error, undefined, JSON.stringify(response)); return response.result;
    }
    async function tool(name, args) {
      const result = await request('tools/call', { name, arguments: args });
      assert.notEqual(result.isError, true, JSON.stringify(result)); return result;
    }
    try {
      await request('initialize', { protocolVersion: '2025-11-25', capabilities: {}, clientInfo: { name: 'guide', version: '1' } });
      assert.equal((await request('tools/list', {})).tools.length, 7);
      await tool('talox_launch', { profileId: 'mcp-lab', profileClass: 'qa', browser: 'chromium' });
      healthy(JSON.parse((await tool('talox_navigate', { url })).content[0].text));
      healthy(JSON.parse((await tool('talox_type', { selector: '#name', text: 'MCP' })).content[0].text));
      healthy(JSON.parse((await tool('talox_click', { selector: '#save' })).content[0].text));
      healthy(JSON.parse((await tool('talox_state', { variant: 'agent' })).content[0].text));
      assert.equal((await tool('talox_screenshot', { selector: '#save' })).content[0].mimeType, 'image/png');
      await tool('talox_stop', {});
    } finally { await session.close(); }
  },
  'mcp-stdio': async () => {
    const child = spawn(process.execPath, [cli, 'mcp'], { cwd: dir, stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'] });
    let stdout = '', stderr = '';
    child.stdout.on('data', data => { stdout += data; }); child.stderr.on('data', data => { stderr += data; });
    const exit = once(child, 'exit');
    child.stdin.end(`${JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 1, method: 'tools/list', params: {} })}\n`);
    const [code] = await exit; assert.equal(code, 0, stderr);
    assert.equal(JSON.parse(stdout.trim()).result.tools.length, 7);
  },
};

const selected = process.argv[2];
if (selected && !Object.hasOwn(examples, selected)) throw new Error(`Unknown recipe: ${selected}`);
let failures = 0;
for (const [id, run] of Object.entries(examples)) {
  if (selected && selected !== id) continue;
  try { await run(); console.log(`${id}\texit=0`); }
  catch (error) { failures++; console.error(`${id}\texit=1\n`, error); }
}
console.log(`Artifacts: ${dir}`);
process.exitCode = failures ? 1 : 0;
```
